I honestly don't think moderation has a whole lot to do with it either way. I can't recall ever leaving a forum because it was either over- or under-moderated. I've always left forums (and many of them over the years) because they've done what all popular forums do sooner or later, and gone to shit.

Forums, at least active and popular ones, have a lifespan. They start out quiet, then, if they're good, they enter a golden age. There'll be enough posters there to keep things interesting, but they're the sort of people who seek out relatively quiet forums, which generally means intelligent people interested in actual discussions and debates. That's far and away the best time to be on any given forum.

But if they're popular, they'll attract assholes of one sort of another over time - trolls, shills, willfully ignorant ideologues, spiteful jackasses, the usual forum trash... At first, there'll just be a few of them, and the community and/or the mods will generally deal with them, but if the community is popular enough, they'll just keep showing up. If the mods aren't active enough at that point and don't bring down the banhammer often enough (and often even when they are and do), then sooner or later, there'll be a sort of "critical mass" of assholes and they'll start circle jerking, and then they're there to stay. And to make matters worse, that drives away some number of the better posters, so the assholes quickly come to represent a greater proportion of the userbase. And that's pretty much it for that forum - it's a downward spiral from there.

Reddit was actually a great demonstration of that, because one could watch it happen over and over. I even had it pretty well pegged - it seemed to hit about the time a sub reached about 15,000 subscribers. That was the point at which there would be so many noxious assholes that the better posters would bail to another sub. Then, if that sub caught on, it was just a matter of time until it happened there too.

Now - to go back to the OP question, I really don't think moderation or the lack thereof makes a whole lot of difference in the long run. Presuming the mods are honorable and decent (which is a pretty big presumption all by itself), I don't think they can stem the tide anyway. At least I've never seen any of them succeed. I've seen them try, but the assholes are just too numerous and too relentless and sooner or later the mods just get tired of dealing with their shit. I have been on a few forums (and still go to them) that are pretty ruthlessly moderated by decent people and they're consistently high quality forums. But those are few and far between, and notably they're relatively small forums. I've never seen that sort of moderation work for long on larger forums.

Thinking about that, that could well be because the mods are sort of like the users, in that the good ones bail because they're sick of dealing with the assholes, so the only people left being mods are assholes themselves.
